questionText:
Which among the following statements are correct about the UN Security
Council?
 
(A) In the UN Security Council, there are five permanent members and ten
non-permanent members.
(B) The permanent members in the UN Security Council have a right to veto
only in certain matters like trade policy and environment issues.
(C) The non-permanent members in the UN Security Council serve for only
one year at a time.
(D) The UN Charter gave the permanent members a privileged position to
bring about stability in the post-World War II world.
 
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.quick: The Security Council has 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members (A), and permanent members were given privileged veto power to ensure post-WWII stability (D). Correct: (A) and (D) only.
solution.concept: The statutory composition, privileged P5 veto power, and structural rationale of the United Nations Security Council.
step_by_step: Core Concept: The statutory composition, privileged P5 veto power, and structural rationale of the United Nations Security Council.

Analysis: Analysis of statements on the UN Security Council:
- (A) Correct: The Council comprises fifteen members: five permanent members (P5: US, Russia, UK, France, China) and ten non-permanent members.
- (B) Incorrect: Permanent members possess a negative veto power over ALL substantive resolutions and decisions, not just trade and environment.
- (C) Incorrect: Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for a term of two years, not one year.
- (D) Correct: The drafters of the UN Charter granted permanent status and veto power to the five victorious powers to preserve great power consensus and global stability.
Hence, statements (A) and (D) only are correct.
Conclusion: Option C is the correct choice.
solution.detailed:
Analysis of statements on the UN Security Council:

- (C) Incorrect: Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for a term of two years, not one year.
- (D) Correct: The drafters of the UN Charter granted permanent status and veto power to the five victorious powers to preserve great power consensus and global stability.
Hence, statements (A) and (D) only are correct.
